subject.title: feat(skills): declarative cron-trigger metadata in SKILL.md frontmatter

question: Should installed SKILL.md content be allowed to declare autonomous schedule/event triggers, and what approval, revocation, and trust boundary must gate that execution?
rationale: Source inspection proves the capability is missing, but code cannot choose whether autonomous execution should live in skill metadata, explicit cron jobs, or a plugin/API surface without a maintainer product and security decision.

options.title: Design permissioned SKILL triggers first
options.body: Define a schema plus operator approval, provenance, revocation, and persistence semantics before implementing schedule/event trigger registration.

options.title: Keep scheduling explicit
options.body: Require operators or plugins to create cron jobs through the existing cron/plugin APIs, and improve docs/audit links instead of letting skills self-register jobs.

options.title: Add documentation-only metadata
options.body: Allow a non-executing trigger_description field for audits now while deferring autonomous scheduler integration to a later design.

recommendation.title: Design permissioned SKILL triggers first
recommendation.body: Define a schema plus operator approval, provenance, revocation, and persistence semantics before implementing schedule/event trigger registration.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent history spans skill docs, plugin/SDK contract documentation, cron docs, and repository vision/security guardrails, making this the best routing candidate for the product/security choice.
